parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks federal and state exposures on a traveller. Entry is the sharpest: the Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where documents cast doubt on sex and to weigh fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, and eight-plus governments issued advisories for trans citizens. Refusal can funnel a traveller into immigration custody, where trans men document beatings, forced labour, solitary and sexual abuse — state-perpetrated and patterned. Nationally, passport markers are restricted and official framing ('radically pro-transgender' in counterterrorism strategy) treats trans people as threat. State-side, facility bans (division expanded to universities May 2026, trespass arrest documented, men's-ward hold) are unremedied, and this unit lacks a hate-crime statute. Mitigation is real but partial: courts have enjoined several orders, a student injunction survives, and identity is not criminalised. Severity of the custody and border chain drives the score into the 0.30s.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, and consideration of fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; X markers halted; travellers report blocked/confiscated passports; eight-plus foreign governments issued advisories for trans citizens.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, with limited waivers; suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Discrepancy at the consular or entry stage can escalate to refusal, then immigration custody under documented abusive conditions.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style treatment restrictions (hair, hormones, psychiatric substitution) from 2026; trans men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; division runs a freeze-frame treatment policy; a trans woman was held 24h in a men's ward after arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented cell-placement, segregation or solitary ruling in the division; bureau's reporting on trans prisoners stopped in 2025, so scope is partly unknown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border refusal or a trespass arrest funnels the traveller into birth-sex custody where the documented abuse pattern operates.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans across 21+ units including government buildings; the division extended its ban to colleges/universities on 15 May 2026; trespass offence in four units with a documented 2025 arrest and handcuffing.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units plus capital have no mapped ban; a national appellate order plus Supreme Court denial of stay (Sept 2025) protects one student; private settings generally unaffected outside six units.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Itinerary-dependent: public buildings, campuses and schools in banning units are unusable by identity; asking-to-leave plus refusal converts to arrest.

care_services.exposure: Executive order framing minor gender-affirming care as mutilation; proposed rule barring public insurance for under-18 trans care; DOJ subpoenaed 20-plus hospitals' minor patient records; LGBTQ youth lifeline services shut.
care_services.protection: Not documented: adult emergency care for visitors is not shown to be restricted, and several orders are enjoined.
care_services.interaction: A visiting minor's care access is uncertain; an emergency could out a traveller to clinicians, but ward rules for visitors are not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; officials frame trans people as threat; 66% public support for birth-sex document laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined; federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises severity of any police encounter and legitimises the facility and document regimes the traveller must navigate.

minors_guardians.exposure: Facility bans reach K-12 and, here, campuses; sports bans (2022) and care bans in 27 units; executive order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition — resident-facing but signals hostility toward trans minors.
minors_guardians.protection: A national injunction protects one student's bathroom access through litigation; courts have blocked several orders.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces the same document scrutiny plus minor-specific care, sports and facility exposure at campuses and schools.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: This unit has no hate-crime statute (confirmed since 2007); only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes; no documented trans-specific violence rate for the unit.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; the dossier documents no trans-specific killings or organised targeting pattern.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assault recourse is uneven depending on whether federal or state charging applies; absence of a violence pattern is thin data, not proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit unresolved; bathroom-law merits undecided; corrections reporting ceased in 2025; a July 2026 assessment flags four 'Do Not Travel' units and continuing degradation; prison placement undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined or blocked multiple national orders; a Supreme Court denial preserved a student injunction; legal-aid FAQ and equality maps track rules in real time.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy availability varies by unit and by month, so exposure is partly a function of travel dates and itinerary.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: a birth-sex facility rule applied to visitors with no exemption and complaints failing to move it. Ours adds documented immigration-custody abuse and a border fraud/lifetime-bar lever, but retains courts that enjoin orders and non-criminalised identity — net roughly equal, arguably a touch lower.

Materially lower. 0.55-B has a working national complaint process, no presentation offence and no custody or border abuse; our dossier documents state-perpetrated custody abuse, entry-refusal exposure with foreign advisories, and an unremedied facility arrest.

Far lower. 0.75-C rests on accepted documents, a dead-letter statute, community acceptance and courts awarding enforced compensation; our record shows active official threat-framing, restrictive document adjudication and unremedied facility exclusion.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is a chain: document discrepancy or a suspected mismatch at entry triggers refusal and possible fraud findings, which can drop a trans traveller into immigration custody where abuse is documented and patterned; if entry succeeds, state facility bans (including this unit's 2026 campus expansion) make gendered spaces unusable, with trespass arrest and a men's-ward hold already recorded. Official framing at the national level treats trans people as threat, while this unit lacks a hate-crime statute. Mitigation is genuine but partial: identity is not criminalised, courts have enjoined several orders, a student injunction survives, and legal-aid guidance exists — enough to keep this above the 0.25 targeting tier, but not enough to offset the custody and border chain, placing the visit in the low-0.3s.
